The security-review specialist reviewed c270201970dbd55bf1f11c9ed3d7d2491c5be8e6..c783985cd54ce4aca0a7f29be16cf0fd93d7e9ab and found no introduced vulnerability. The direct-child/last-value config-parser changes and associated tests/docs add no security blocker. No outstanding R1 security finding existed; functional R260-001 closure remains with the correctness reviewer. No new C34 hardening follow-up is raised.

The R1 nonblocking global-state caveat remains: invoking installed OMP config get is not provably read-only on persistent settings/storage, even though project-to-global config linkage is not introduced. I did not run the live OMP sensor or change global configuration. C33 still treats the same-user execution environment as trusted.

IMPORTANT FINALITY FAILURE: just pr-freeze 260 returned exit 1 during this review, NOT FINAL, because merge status is now DIRTY (conflicts with main). This differs from the earlier FINAL packet. Remote and GitHub still agree on the exact requested head, the detached worktree is clean, and CI check (22), check (24), rust-lint, rust-test and Delivers all pass. Main base, ready status and unchanged migration numbering also passed. The coder/PM must resolve the main conflict and rerun pr-freeze before treating the PR as final. This exact-head security verdict is not merge readiness or approval of a subsequent head.

Validation limits: static security review only; no local tests, builds, cargo commands, dependency installations, OMP commands, credential-file reads or global-config changes. Just recipes were not prefixed with nice.
